messages:
eve_customer: Hey team — we rolled 30% traffic to dedicated this morning and now our indexer is failing. Embedding vectors are sometimes length 128 instead of 512, causing downstream shape errors.

alice_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the failing request/response (please redact API keys)?

eve_customer: here's a minimal repro (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer redacted' \n  -d '{"model":"embeddings-prod","input":"hello"}'
```
and sample response we logged: `{\n  "data": [ { "embedding": [0.12, 0.03, ...] } ], \n  "shape": 128 \n}`

alice_support: thanks. two quick checks: are you using an alias that might map to different model variants across Hosted vs Dedicated? also, any batching middleware in front of the client?

eve_customer: no batching on client. we do have a proxy that adds an Authorization header depending on env. We didn't touch the alias.

deploy-bot: Deployment finished: dedicated/cluster-dd-23 (canary->stable) :white_check_mark:

tom_sre: Paging in SRE — see similar symptoms last month when a stale model alias pointed to a legacy 128-dim embed model during traffic split. Could be routing policy (smart routing) sending some requests to older model instance.

maria_ml: Agree. If the control plane routing table had stale entries for the dedicated pool, requests with certain customer tokens got routed to `embed-lite-128`. Can you share a request id from the log?

eve_customer: request id `req_20260315_92a` (from our logs). We see it hitting a dedicated endpoint: `dedicated-12.prod.redwood`

nate_eng: grabbing platform logs now — early signal: the auth token in that request was issued before the recent alias migration. The token-to-tenant mapping logic has a cached model mapping TTL (30m) that didn't invalidate correctly during the deploy.

alice_support: ok that explains parity mismatch (Hosted expecting 512, Dedicated returning 128). Short-term workaround: rotate tokens for affected clients or pin the request to explicit model `embeddings-v2-512` until we flush mappings.

maria_ml: Also worth checking batching behavior on the dedicated runtime: if a batched request mixes inputs for different pinned models, the runtime can fall back or interleave—leading to shape coercion or truncated vectors. Config snippet to inspect: `batch_size: 32, max_latency_ms: 40, allowed_model_aliases: ["embeddings-v2-512"]`.

tom_sre: I pushed a config to flush model mapping cache on the dedicated control plane and restarted the routing agent. Monitoring now for 15m.

nate_eng: I've queued a job to re-issue short-lived tokens for the affected org and will post when done.

eve_customer: thanks. one more question — we also saw intermittent 429s earlier. Is that related?

alice_support: likely related: the canary bumped autoscaler and temporarily saturated the dedicated pool causing rejects; also some requests routed to a lighter model reduced throughput but not capacity, producing odd rate-limit signals. We'll correlate traces.

maria_ml: Follow-up action items: 1) Confirm token rotation resolves parity (blocking). 2) Ensure model alias mappings are invalidated during rollout (SRE). 3) Add assertion in runtime to reject cross-model batched inputs (ENG). 4) Postmortem if increased customer error rates > 0.5% for 1h.

alice_support: Eve, we'll keep you updated in this thread. If you can do token rotation now we can validate immediately. :thumbsup:

eve_customer: rotating tokens now, will update in ~5m. Thanks all.

(threads and traces will be attached to the ticket 5823)
